feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR National News for reporting across the United States. Explore coverage of economic affordability, immigration, climate, environmental policy, justice and social trends.

entry.title: Crews search for survivors after deadly Brooklyn building collapse
entry.summary: A three-story apartment building in Brooklyn collapsed, killing at least eight people and injuring two dozen others.

entry.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
entry.summary: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

entry.title: Kennedy Center plans Ticketmaster switch, raising conflict of interest concerns
entry.summary: The Kennedy Center's former president Richard Grenell was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's parent company at the same time the two parties were negotiating.

entry.title: White House warns Trump probes could be criminal. Rep. Robert Garcia won't back down
entry.summary: Incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman Robert Garcia says Democrats won't be intimidated by White House threats over their planned investigations: "It's in the Constitution."

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi, The White House is getting ready to fight new Democratic oversight, U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine have wrapped up.

entry.title: Some states get a head start on upcoming federal hemp ban
entry.summary: A federal ban on Hemp-derived THC products is set to take effect in less than a month. But some states have moved to start their own ban earlier.

entry.title: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
entry.summary: The SS United States broke trans-Atlantic speed records. On Wednesday, it was sunk off the Florida coast and will become a diving destination and home for marine life.

entry.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
entry.summary: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

entry.title: The legacy of the 1991 Gulf War and the Americans who carried out the mission
entry.summary: 35 years since the Gulf War ended, veterans reflect on the conflict and its ongoing impact.

entry.title: A Kennedy relative talks about his family's lawsuit against Trump's 250-foot arch
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Max Kennedy, son of Robert Kennedy Sr., about the Kennedy family's lawsuit to halt the construction of President Trump's 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery.
